prompt: Holden places five paper slips with the numbers $1$ through $5$ written on them into a bag, and draws them out one by one, at random and without replacement. He lets the first slip drawn be $a$, the second be $b$, the third be $c$, the fourth be $d$, and the fifth be $e$. Find the expected value of $10(ab+bc+cd+de+ea)$.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
By linearity, each of the five products $ab,bc,cd,de,ea$ is the product of two distinct random slips, with the same expectation. For two distinct slips drawn from $1,\dots,5$: $E[xy]=\frac{(\sum x)^2-\sum x^2}{5\cdot4}=\frac{225-55}{20}=\frac{17}{2}$. So the expectation of the sum is $5\cdot\frac{17}2=\frac{85}2$, and $10\cdot\frac{85}2=425$.

**Answer: 425**

prompt: There exist four primes $p,q,r,s$ with $p>q$ and $r>s$ such that $(p+q)(r+s)+(p-q)(r-s)=100$. Find $p+q+r+s$.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Expanding, $(p+q)(r+s)+(p-q)(r-s)=2pr+2qs$, so $pr+qs=50$. Since $p>q\ge2$ and $r>s\ge2$, $p$ and $r$ are odd, so $pr$ is odd, hence $qs$ is odd and all four primes are odd: $p,r\ge5$, $q,s\ge3$. Then $pr\ge25$ and $qs\ge9$, so $pr\in\{25,35\}$ (odd products of two primes at least $5$ not exceeding $41$). If $pr=25$ then $p=r=5$, $q,s=3$ and $qs=9\ne25$. If $pr=35$ then $\{p,r\}=\{5,7\}$ and $qs=15$ means $\{q,s\}=\{3,5\}$ with $q<p$, $s<r$: $(p,q,r,s)=(5,3,7,5)$ or $(7,5,5,3)$. In both cases $p+q+r+s=20$.

**Answer: 20**
